blocks.instruction: Leia o texto e escolha a alternativa correta. Algumas perguntas pedem inferência — a resposta não está escrita com todas as letras.
blocks.passage:
At executive level, corporate tax is a strategic variable alongside cost, price and capital. It shapes how much of a company's value reaches shareholders, how much gets reinvested, and how much is quietly transferred to the governments where the company operates. The senior leader's task is not to minimise it — that is a narrow view — but to understand its shape and to make sure that shape matches the company's long-term strategy.

A company with a stable effective tax rate is easier to value, easier to forecast, and easier to explain to investors. A company with a volatile rate is immediately less trusted, even when the volatility is entirely honest. Stability, here, is worth a small premium.

I would recommend that every senior finance leader treat corporate tax as a managed variable, not a received result. The companies that do achieve steady, predictable outcomes over long periods. The companies that do not live with surprise every quarter — and quietly pay the cost of that surprise in how the market values them.

items.q: According to the text, what is the senior leader's task regarding corporate tax?
options: To keep it invisible to investors
To transfer as much value as possible to shareholders
To minimise it as aggressively as possible
To understand its shape and align it with long-term strategy
items.why: "not to minimise it… but to understand its shape and to make sure that shape matches the company's long-term strategy."

items.q: Why is a stable effective tax rate described as worth a small premium?
options: Because it lowers the total tax paid
Because it makes the company easier to value, forecast and explain
Because it eliminates all quarterly surprises
items.why: "easier to value, easier to forecast, and easier to explain to investors… Stability, here, is worth a small premium."

items.q: The text suggests that a volatile tax rate is penalised by the market even when…
items.why: Inferência: "less trusted, even when the volatility is entirely honest" — o mercado penaliza a imprevisibilidade em si, não a má-fé.

items.q: Which statement would the author most likely DISAGREE with?
options: Tax outcomes influence how the market values a company.
The right goal for a finance leader is simply to pay as little tax as legally possible.
Predictability of the tax rate carries real value for investors.
Corporate tax should be treated as a managed variable.
items.why: Inferência: o autor chama a pura minimização de "a narrow view" — discordaria de reduzir tudo a pagar o mínimo.

items.q: What does "quietly pay the cost of that surprise" most likely imply?
options: The company pays a hidden fine to the government
The cost appears as a lower valuation rather than an obvious line item
Shareholders are paid less in dividends by law
items.why: Inferência: "quietly… in how the market values them" — o custo é uma avaliação mais baixa, não uma cobrança explícita.

blocks.instruction: Ouça Sophie apresentando o plano de três anos ao conselho e aos investidores. Responda sem ler a transcrição — ela só aparece depois de corrigir.

audio.text:
Thank you all for making the time. What I'm putting in front of you today is a three-year plan, and I want to be very clear about what it is — and what it isn't.

It is not a plan to make our tax rate lower. If our headline number stays exactly where it is, but stops jumping around every quarter, I will consider this a success. Because what you, as investors, are really paying for is not the number itself — it is being able to trust the number. A rate that moves three points one way and four points the other tells the market that we don't fully understand our own business.

So the work is unglamorous. We are cleaning up how we recognise deferred items, aligning the timing of a few large deductions, and settling two open positions across jurisdictions so they stop surprising us. None of this is aggressive. None of it is clever. It is simply about turning a received result into a managed one.

I would recommend we hold our nerve on this for the full three years. The temptation, every quarter, will be to chase a slightly lower rate. I'd ask you to resist that with me — because the premium we're building here is trust, and trust is only ever earned slowly.
audio.label: Ouça quantas vezes precisar. A transcrição aparece depois de corrigir.

items.q: What would Sophie consider a success for this plan?
options: Raising the rate to reassure regulators
Keeping the rate roughly where it is but stopping it from jumping around
Cutting the headline tax rate significantly
items.why: "If our headline number stays exactly where it is, but stops jumping around every quarter, I will consider this a success."

items.q: According to Sophie, what are investors really paying for?
options: Being able to trust the number
items.why: "what you… are really paying for is not the number itself — it is being able to trust the number."

items.q: Which of these did Sophie list as part of the work?
options: Relocating the head office to a lower-tax country
Aligning the timing of a few large deductions
Launching an aggressive new tax structure
items.why: "aligning the timing of a few large deductions, and settling two open positions across jurisdictions."

items.q: What does Sophie mean by "turning a received result into a managed one"?
options: Letting the market decide the rate
Outsourcing the tax function to advisers
Taking active control of an outcome that used to just happen to them
items.why: Inferência: passar de sofrer o número que aparece a governar deliberadamente o resultado.

items.q: Why does Sophie ask the investors to "hold their nerve" for three years?
options: Because the board might replace her
Because the rate will rise sharply first
Because there will be a recurring temptation to chase a slightly lower rate, which would undo the trust being built
Because the plan is legally risky
items.why: Inferência: ela alerta que a cada trimestre haverá a tentação de perseguir uma taxa menor, e cede a isso destruiria o prêmio de confiança.

blocks.instruction: O vocabulário da lição aparece aqui em frases novas. Escolha o sentido ou a palavra que cabe no contexto.

items.q: "The board now treats tax as a strategic variable, not an afterthought." A strategic variable is…
options: a factor management can shape to influence long-term direction
a fixed legal obligation that cannot be altered
items.why: Strategic variable = variável estratégica: algo que a gestão modela para orientar o rumo, não um dado imutável.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "Rather than distribute the gain, the group chose to ___ it in new capacity."
items.why: To reinvest = reinvestir: aplicar o ganho de volta no negócio em vez de distribuí-lo.

items.q: "Judging tax purely by the rate is a narrow view." A narrow view is…
options: a limited perspective that misses the bigger picture
items.why: Narrow view = visão estreita: uma perspectiva limitada que ignora o quadro completo.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "Investors distrust a ___ rate that swings unpredictably from quarter to quarter."
items.why: Volatile = volátil: que oscila de forma imprevisível — o oposto de stable.

items.q: "A predictable outcome commands a premium from the market." Here premium means…
options: an extra value or higher price the market is willing to pay
items.why: Premium = prêmio: o valor adicional que o mercado paga por estabilidade e confiança.

blocks.instruction: Expressões que aparecem em reuniões de estratégia tributária. Escolha o sentido no contexto.

items.q: "The audit committee still has to sign off on the tax provision." To sign off on means to…
items.why: Sign off on = aprovar formalmente, dar o aval final.

items.q: "We'll roll out the new provisioning process across all entities next year." To roll out means to…
items.why: Roll out = implementar de forma progressiva, por etapas.

items.q: "The regional CFOs pushed back on the timing of the deductions." They…
items.why: Push back on = resistir, discordar — sem necessariamente rejeitar de vez.

items.q: "They agreed the rate-stabilisation plan but never followed through." They…
options: failed to carry it to completion
items.why: Follow through = levar até o fim o que foi combinado; aqui, o oposto aconteceu.

items.q: "Shaving half a point off the rate won't move the needle on how investors see us." This means it will…
items.why: Move the needle = mexer o ponteiro, fazer diferença perceptível — aqui, não fará.
